# N71 personal access token entry (brief for Codex)

**Owner decision (2026-11-24):** the leader types a Planning Center personal access token (PAT) into the app for each session. The token is held in memory only. It is never stored, logged, exported, put in History or Undo, sent to analytics, or written into any tracked file or fixture. Do not run any live request against Planning Center; the owner will test live.

**Run after** the N3 fix run (brief: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-24-n3-release-fixes.md`) has finished and its changes are reviewed, so the two runs do not edit the same files.

**Model:** GPT Astra, Medium effort (security-sensitive implementation).

**Rules (AGENTS.md):** no commit, no push. Run only the closest test files or `--node-only`. No real names or personal data in code, fixtures, or docs. Keep `dev/app/drive-config.js` empty.

## Step 0: verify the auth format before coding

Read the official authentication documentation for Planning Center personal access tokens: https://api.planningcenteronline.com/docs/overview/authentication. Confirm the header format (the existing code assumes Bearer, which is the OAuth format; a PAT is expected to use HTTP Basic with app ID and secret). If the docs say otherwise, follow the docs and report the difference. Do not guess. If the docs cannot be read, stop and report.

## Required behaviour

- A PAT entry form appears in the Planning Center panel only (the N71 registrations area). The key is stored by the leader's browser password manager, which fills the form. Use a real `<form>` with a username field (the PAT ID, if the leader wants it saved alongside) and a `type="password"` secret field with `autocomplete="current-password"` so the browser's password manager can fill and save it. The app must never write the value anywhere itself. Read the value into memory on submit, then clear the field. The field is also cleared when the panel closes, when the file changes, and when the leader presses a Forget button.
- The app itself must not persist the key. The browser's own password manager is the only store. Document this in the panel's help text: "Your browser's password manager stores this key, not the app."
- The token lives in a module-scope variable only. No `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB, cookies, files, History, Undo, drive saves, logs, error messages, or exports. Do not include the token in any error text or URL.
- Requests go only to the existing allowlisted API origin and the allowlisted collection paths. Use GET only. Refuse any other method, origin, or path.
- Existing OAuth code stays in place, inert, and untouched except where it must share a helper. Do not enable OAuth sign-in.
- Responses are handled by the existing pagination and completeness checks. A 401 or 403 clears the token from memory and shows a clear "token rejected" message.
- Do not add a live path to Check-Ins (N72) in this brief. N72 remains local-only.

## Tests (pure Node, no network)

- Header construction matches the documented format; the token never appears in a URL or in any string passed to logging helpers.
- The token is not present in saved file data, History, Undo, or export output after entry (use a sentinel value and assert absence).
- Forget, file switch, and panel close clear the token.
- A non-GET request or a non-allowlisted origin or path is refused before any fetch.
- A 401 response clears the token and reports rejection without echoing it.

Use only invented sentinel values such as `TEST-pat-id` and `TEST-pat-secret`.

## Report back

Files changed, tests added and run (names and results), the auth format the docs confirmed, anything skipped and why, and the `git status --short` output. Do not commit.
